# Verification analysis: redundant-uplinks-ubuntu16

Job: `2026-09-05__03-00-00`

This report explains the verifier decisions recorded for this job. It interprets the saved evidence; it does not rerun the task or independently inspect the expired clusters.

## Task

> `node1` and `node2` are joined by two independent links, and each serves a
> private network holding one host, `node3` and `node4`. Carry traffic between
> the two private networks over both links, and keep `node3` and `node4`
> reaching each other when either one of the links is taken out of service.

- Systems: **2 sonic + 2 ubuntu16.04**
- Networks: **mgmt, transit-a, transit-b, lan-a, lan-b**
- Control node: **node3**
- Executor model: **claude-sonnet-5**

## Trial `redundant-uplinks-ubuntu16__wiuw6Rz`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** All material outcomes of the task instruction are satisfied with direct evidence: a genuine dual-link (balance-rr bond) fabric carries traffic between node1 and node2 (proven by per-link tx counters), node3 and node4 reach each other across it, and connectivity survives a live, bounded outage of one physical link with 0% packet loss followed by restoration. The independently-required provider-wide restart protocol was also completed and evidenced for all four nodes, each showing pre-restart health, a restart acknowledgement, a changed boot identity, and full post-restart recovery of bonding, routing, and end-to-end connectivity, cross-checked against the fixed after-executor boot-identity snapshots. Operational hygiene is good: the one wasted attempt (LACP bonding that never converged) was fully superseded with no residue, and various discovery-phase temporary IP assignments were cleanly removed or overwritten.

| Reward | Coverage | Functionality | Hygiene | Confidence | Commands |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.850 | 0.900 | 77/5 (+7 dropped) |

### Why the verifier reached this decision

- **dual-link-bond — Satisfied:** Both independent links between node1 and node2 (eth1, eth2) are used to carry traffic between the two private networks
  - **Why:** Executor empirically identified eth1/eth2 as the two node1-node2 links, built a balance-rr Linux bond0 over both on each SONiC node, and verified via per-interface tx/rx counters that both eth1 and eth2 actively carried packets during a 20-ping burst (cmd-f49728a2d6ad40b5 before, cmd-8046b5d55ba04bc8 after: eth1 +10, eth2 +10 tx_packets). Routes for 192.168.10.0/24 and 192.168.20.0/24 were installed via bond0 on each side (cmd-4d2c0f6714814b94, cmd-d971e26ce2114898).
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-87c65d98d75c4ce6`, `cmd-76b5b2e18c0b403b`, `cmd-4d2c0f6714814b94`, `cmd-d971e26ce2114898`, `cmd-f49728a2d6ad40b5`, `cmd-dabf7f64871e443b`, `cmd-8046b5d55ba04bc8`
- **node3-node4-reachability — Satisfied:** node3 and node4, each behind node1/node2 respectively, can reach each other
  - **Why:** node3 (192.168.10.12/24) and node4 (192.168.20.13/24) were configured with routes to each other's subnet via node1/node2, and bidirectional pings succeeded with 0% loss (cmd-3ad8b8af04664393, cmd-6549d9574bb445b2).
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-c7e2c8a9a3aa415b`, `cmd-e8f3d19a33b84ac0`, `cmd-3ad8b8af04664393`, `cmd-6549d9574bb445b2`
- **link-failover — Satisfied:** node3/node4 keep reaching each other when either link between node1 and node2 is taken out of service

The link was then restored and traffic resumed on eth1 (tx count rose 109->139, cmd-317e4e202723435e, cmd-d220398e53554c23, cmd-09dba2f21de04266), completing the healthy-baseline -> disruption -> recovery transition. Only the eth1 link was explicitly tested (not eth2), but given the symmetric balance-rr bonding this is adequate evidence for 'either link.'

### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.850**. One notable unnecessary-but-bounded mutation: the executor first configured bond0 in 802.3ad LACP mode on both node1 and node2 (cmd-2d440a3c7f2046f6, cmd-c902e5b9fd314da7), which never converged since the links are direct point-to-point virtio connections with no LACPDU relay — a plausible but ultimately failed approach. It was fully superseded (bond0 deleted and rebuilt) by the working balance-rr script moments later (cmd-6d2a733b09f44622, cmd-b19b05dbf2f44b13), leaving no residue. Several temporary /31 probe addresses were added to eth1/eth2/eth3/ens7 for link discovery and manually removed within the same or a following command (cmd-87c65d98d75c4ce6, cmd-76b5b2e18c0b403b, cmd-8292a417e44245ff, cmd-1f728f8e8fc24e23 removed by cmd-127834f2ca11497b, cmd-04bc80bde36c4fbf/cmd-e9031d6f447b41fc later flushed by cmd-c7e2c8a9a3aa415b/cmd-e8f3d19a33b84ac0) — all bounded, low-risk, and reverted or superseded by final configuration. No unauthorized package changes, no exposed services beyond SONiC's normal set, and package-health/failed-services snapshots show only pre-existing conditions (system-health.service and watchdog-control.service were already failed before any executor action). Persistence was correctly installed via an enabled systemd oneshot unit and ifupdown drop-ins.

Hygiene evidence: `cmd-2d440a3c7f2046f6`, `cmd-c902e5b9fd314da7`, `cmd-6d2a733b09f44622`, `cmd-b19b05dbf2f44b13`, `cmd-87c65d98d75c4ce6`, `cmd-76b5b2e18c0b403b`, `cmd-1f728f8e8fc24e23`, `cmd-127834f2ca11497b`, `cmd-04bc80bde36c4fbf`, `cmd-e9031d6f447b41fc`, `cmd-c7e2c8a9a3aa415b`, `cmd-e8f3d19a33b84ac0`, `global:before_prepare:node1:failed-services`, `global:after_executor:node1:failed-services`

### Comments and limitations

- Only the eth1 link was explicitly failure-tested; eth2 failover was not independently demonstrated, though the symmetric balance-rr configuration and post-recovery evidence make this a minor gap.
- The failover test downed eth1 on both node1 and node2 in the same step rather than isolating a single physical link failure; this correctly represents that link going out of service, but the trace does not separately show carrier-loss-only detection on one side without an administrative action on the peer.
- Operational hygiene was below a full pass (0.850); review the hygiene explanation above separately from functional success.
- Verifier confidence was 0.900; this is evidence confidence for this trial, not a repeatability estimate.
